question: For Outfall 001, does the authorization to discharge storm runoffs from storage and production areas, once-through cooling water, cleaning water, and Artesian well water establish that monitoring obligations and enforceable numeric discharge limits apply only when one or more of these specifically authorized discharge types is occurring at that outfall?
semantic_arguments: The authorization sentence enumerates four distinct discharge categories rather than a single undifferentiated effluent.
Purpose A requires distinguishing enforceable numeric limits from monitoring for which no numeric compliance comparison is applicable.
Purpose B evaluates monitoring requirements that depend on discharge occurrence and other permit conditions.
Purpose C distinguishes documented no-discharge periods and conditional monitoring from other missing-evidence states.
The Outfall 001 pollutant table lists uniform limits and monitoring frequencies without expressly conditioning each row on which authorized discharge type is active.
Adjacent WET testing footnote (2) ties at least one monitoring requirement to discharge occurrence ('at first discharge').
notes: Different readings of whether obligations attach per authorized discharge type versus per outfall regardless of active stream would change applicability determinations, unresolved-case handling, and whether numeric compliance comparisons are in scope for a given monitoring period.
